metadata.title: Security Banned Group Patterns
metadata.description: Patterns for banned-group support, normalization, and recruitment.

concepts.title: Terrorism
concepts.description: Promotion, support, glorification, or operational discussion of terrorism.

concepts.title: Extremism
concepts.description: Support for extremist ideology or extremist violence.

concepts.title: State Institutions
concepts.description: Government institutions, state authority, and public order bodies.

entries.title: Banned Group Support
entries.description: Language that sympathizes with, normalizes, or recruits for a banned group.
supporting_evidence: A positive label is attached to the banned group.
The line invites participation or support.
contradictory_evidence: The sentence is clearly framed as condemnation.
A report repeats the group name only as evidence.
false_positives: A journalist identifying the group as banned.
A fictional antihero quoting the group to mock it.
counter_examples: Court evidence mentioning the group name.
cross_sentence_indicators: A neutral sentence is followed by a supportive phrase.
reviewer_guidance: Check whether the group is praised, normalized, or invited.
Use context to separate reporting from support.

confidence_modifiers.title: Direct Invite
confidence_modifiers.description: Explicit invitation to join or support.

confidence_modifiers.title: Coded Admiration
confidence_modifiers.description: Subtle admiration for a banned group.

glossary_relationships.note: Support for banned groups often overlaps extremism.
Banned groups commonly target state institutions.

gcam_mappings.note: Use for recruitment or sympathy language.

examples.title: Support phrase
examples.expected_outcome: Direct praise of a banned group.
